title: api-config-runtime-arch-scratch-jamie
content:
Quick scratchpad: runtime API config shape + routing + KV/cache interaction.

Goal: capture a minimal, implementable config schema that lets the router pick runtime behaviours (batching, cache policy, RT priority, model variant fallbacks) per-route while keeping global safety and quotas. This is a living draft - focusing on fields we need for Dedicated/private as well as hosted.

Open questions (high pri):
- How much of this should be per-tenant vs per-route? (thinking: tenant-level defaults + route overrides)
- Do we encode quantization/precision in routing policy or as model variant metadata?
- Fallback semantics: cascade order should be explicit (primary -> variant -> degraded model -> queued) and include SLA hints.

Proposed config shape (pseudo-yaml/plain text):

route_config:
  id: string (route name)
  tenant_id: string? (optional override)
  model_selector:
    preferred_model: string (model-id:version)
    fallback_models: [string] (ordered)
    allow_quantized: boolean
  scheduling:
    priority: low|normal|high
    max_latency_ms: int?
    batch_policy:
      enabled: true|false
      max_batch_size: int
      max_wait_ms: int
  cache_policy:
    enabled: true|false
    type: prefix|kv|response
    ttl_ms: int
    kv_cache_hint: hot|warm|cold
  telemetry:
    sampling_rate: float (0..1)
    perf_tracing: true|false
  cost_control:
    max_tokens_per_minute: int
    cost_budget_cents_per_hour: int

Notes on fields:
- model_selector.allow_quantized: used by router to pick quantized variant if available + tenant allows it. Separate from model metadata so we can route to quantized bundles without changing client model-id.
- cache_policy.kv_cache_hint: hint to runtime about how aggressively to checkpoint KV to shared store (hot = keep local longer, warm = evict earlier).
- scheduling.batch_policy: defaults should be tuned by tenant tier. "max_wait_ms" trades latency vs cost; some routes should set to 0 for strict SLO.

Router decision flow (sketch):

Client -> API GW -> Auth & Quotas -> Route Lookup (route_config) -> Policy Eval -> Candidate model list -> Capacity check (region/pool) -> Select model instance -> Apply cache lookup -> If cache hit: serve from cache; otherwise enqueue into batcher -> runtime executes -> store to cache if eligible -> respond

ASCII diagram:

  [Client]
     |
     v
  [API-GW]
     | auth/quota
     v
  [Router] --(route_config)-> [Policy Engine]
     |
     v
 [Capacity Checker] -> [Model Pool: GPU nodes] -> [Runtime Executor]
            ^                                |
            |                                v
         [KV Cache] <------------------ [KV checkpoint/evict]

Telemetry / Tracing notes:
- Emit token-level latency histogram + per-route batch size distribution.
- Tag traces with route_id, tenant_id, model_id, fallback_used.

Fallback semantics (proposal):
1) If primary model not available within "max_latency_ms" budget and fallback_models provided, try in order.
2) If no compatible model available in region, apply cross-region fallback only if tenant allows.
3) If still no model, apply degraded path: respond with partial result via a cheaper reranker or return 503 depending on route policy.

Implementation concerns / TODOs:
- Need a schema registry for route_config (versioned). Ensure runtime can read old configs for a rollout.
- Migration plan: add "batch_policy" defaults in platform console + gradual rollout to avoid perf cliffs.
- Add unit tests for policy engine: prioritization, fallback order, cache TTL enforcement.
- Perf: measure overhead of policy eval per req; aim <1ms median.

Short term next steps:
- Iterate this shape with Casey & Priya (week of Nov 17).
- Wire up a playground route that exercises quantized fallback and KV caching.
- Draft Confluence page that formalizes migration & API contract (link will be added).

Notes-to-self: keep route_config compact. If we add too many knobs, UX will suffer. Provide good defaults per tenant tier and expose advanced toggles in console.

References / links to previous sketches: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-4821, JIRA-INF-1037, PR #289 in serving-runtime.

-- jamie
